authoring.batches_composed_with: a scratch typing aid outside the repository (not committed); the committed batches are the authored inputs, each applied by the seed's edit, then verify, resolve and build
authoring.kernel_base_note: a SPIR-V build request made with the Python reference constructors (benchmarks.spirv_kernels.collatz_kernel and build_request); the native edit interface has no operation that gives a request a non-Windows target, so the kernel function F0 is replaced natively (define and replace) on this store

claim: An XAX Windows program (a native batch on integration/windows_helpers/hash_request.xax) loads a SPIR-V module from standard input and drives vulkan-1.dll through win64-c foreign declarations: instance, physical device, device, three storage buffers, shader module, compute pipeline, descriptor set, command buffer, dispatch, queue submit, map and read back. The module is built by the production compiler (native Windows seed) from a kernel authored as a native batch.

controls.empty_stdin: no SPIR-V on standard input: exit status 2 before any Vulkan call
controls.mutated_kernel: one native edit (const N11 3266489910) on the kernel: 16383 of 16384 records differ from the CPU result on the RTX 3060, so the comparison detects a wrong kernel

cpu_oracle.language: Python, scratch, outside the repository (the formula is in kernel.function and kernel.input)

evidence_label: EXECUTED on GPU hardware (RTX 3060 Laptop GPU and AMD Radeon iGPU); device output equals an independent CPU computation

executables.device_index_1_is: the device_index_0 store with vkhost_device1.batch applied by the seed's edit (const N81 1, const N87 24)

host.run_with: Start-Process -RedirectStandardInput kernel.spv -RedirectStandardOutput out.bin (cmd /c file redirection makes the existing hash host fail too)

kernel.function: per invocation i: h = 0x811C9DC5; for the 16 words w of record i: h = rotr(h ^ w, 13) * 0x85EBCA6B + 0xC2B2AE35; then h ^= rotr(h, 16); h *= 0x27D4EB2F; h ^= rotr(h, 15); out[i] = h (32-bit wrap)
kernel.input: generated by the host: x0 = 12345, x(k+1) = x(k) * 1664525 + 1013904223 mod 2^32, word j = x(j+1)
kernel.name: record fingerprint

limits: one kernel (an integer record hash); no floats, atomics, barriers or 64-bit integers in the kernel
Windows host only; Vulkan objects are not destroyed (the process exits); a single dispatch; no timing
the SPIR-V base request store is made with Python reference constructors; the kernel body and both host programs are native batches
the host reads the SPIR-V module with one ReadFile of redirected standard input (up to 16384 bytes)
no performance claim: no GPU timing or comparison arm was measured
output_layout: 67584 bytes on standard output: VkPhysicalDeviceProperties (824 bytes at 0), the status binding word at 0x400 (0 = no trap), 16384 result words at 0x800
